messages.author: 43bbffc192263b0d
messages.subject: GOF test for gdistremoval models
parts:
Hi all,

I am wondering what the best way is to assess Goodness of fit for models fit with gdistremoval. 

The data structure: I have three seasons of point count data where I visited each site only once. I have 'stacked the years so that I have a total of 910 sites with only one visit. At each point I recorded both distance and time of detection which I binned and used for the yDistance and yRemoval arguments in my unmarkedFrameGDR. I have been able to run all my models but have trouble using the parboot function.

Before the gdistremoval function was released I was using gdistsamp and used the user-defined function:

fitstats <- function(fm) {
  observed <- getY(fm@data)
  expected <- fitted(fm)
  resids <- residuals(fm)
  sse <- sum(resids^2)
  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
  return(out)
}

pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=10, report=1)

This worked well for gdistsamp, but I realized I can't use this exact function this with gdistremoval because 1) getY(fm@data) returns only the yRemoval data and 2) fitted(fm) and residuals(fm) return a list of 2 matrices (one for dist and one for rem) that can not be squared or divided by etc.

I have tried manipulating the function a number of ways but have not had any luck getting it to work with parboot. Has anyone else found a good way to asses goodness of fit for gdistremoval models, either using parboot or other? 

in case it helps, this is one example of what I tried:

fm<-<-gdistremoval(lambdaformula=~1, phiformula=~1, removalformula=~1, distanceformula=~1, BRSPumf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="abund", unitsOut="ha", mixture = "ZIP", engine = "TMB")

fitstats <- function(fm) {
  observed <- list(dist = fm@data@yDistance, rem = fm@data@yRemoval)
  observed<-cbind(observed$dist, observed$rem)
  expected <- fitted(fm)
  expected<-cbind(expected$dist, expected$rem)
  resids <- residuals(fm)
  resids<- cbind(resids$dist, resids$rem)
  sse <- sum(resids^2)
  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
  return(out)
}

This works if you run it outside of parboot, but I get an error  when I run:
pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=10, report=1)

Error in t.star[i, ] : subscript out of bounds

Thanks for any advice, sorry for the long email...

Katie

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: GOF test for gdistremoval models
parts:
Here's a version that should work:

fitstats <- function(fm) {
  # Removal
  obs_rem <- fm@data@yRemoval
  exp_rem <- fitted(fm)$rem
 
  chisq_rem <- sum((obs_rem - exp_rem)^2 / exp_rem)
  sse_rem <- sum(residuals(fm)$rem^2)
  freetuke_rem <- sum((sqrt(obs_rem) - sqrt(exp_rem))^2)

  # Distance
  obs_dist <- fm@data@yDistance
  exp_dist <- fitted(fm)$dist
 
  chisq_dist <- sum((obs_dist - exp_dist)^2 / exp_dist)
  sse_dist <- sum(residuals(fm)$dist^2)
  freetuke_dist <- sum((sqrt(obs_dist) - sqrt(exp_dist))^2)

  c(SSE=sse_rem + sse_dist, Chisq = chisq_rem + chisq_dist,
    freemanTukey=freetuke_rem + freetuke_dist)
}

I'm not sure if this is actually a valid way to check the fit of this model considering the two separate detection components - maybe better to look at the stats for each detection model separately?

Ken

Thanks again for taking the time to help!

Katie

Based on that warning message it looks like unmarked is not able to fit the model most or all simulated datasets. What does the actual fitted output from the model look like?

If you have some really large/uncertain parameter estimates that can often cause this type of issue. Or maybe there's some bug in the data simulation code, but it's hard to tell without seeing the model output.

Ken

Thank you so much for your help!!
